limits: Default deterministic third-map seed only; no claim about all seeds or optimal play.
Eight successful third-map simulations prove legal strategies, not depth, balance, cooperation or aesthetic quality.
The lower breach removes a rear-field screen, not all protection of the base. Five base bricks remain in the 50/100ms examples.
200ms breach can remove extra base cover while still winning; it is recorded rather than presented as identical to 100ms.
Damage events cannot attribute every removed brick to a bullet owner; removed tiles are world changes, while central gate entry and explicit breach actions show actual route use.
hashBoundary: hashes bind normalized Git/published blobs; workingCopyHashes preserve the exact Windows candidate files tested. Differences are CRLF normalization only; parsed levels and unchanged engine rules are identical.
